subject: EdgeFin: Performance SLO benchmark methodology - follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@edgefin.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeFin: Performance SLO benchmark methodology - follow-up

Hi Laura — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our call so we're aligned before running the benchmark: 

1) SLO targets you shared: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 150ms, p99 < 250ms for 1k-token streaming responses (we've noted the streaming requirement).
2) Throughput/concurrency target: sustain 120 concurrent sessions at 10 RPS average per session (bursty peaks to 25 RPS/session for short periods).
3) Model mix: primary model is an open LLM (7B quantized) for most traffic; can fail over to a 13B variant for quality-sensitive routes.

To move forward we need:
- The prompt sets you mentioned (representative user traffic, ~200 prompts across short/long/interactive).
- Any pre- and post-processing steps we must apply to reproduce your production stack.
- Confirmation if token streaming is required end-to-end (chunk size, delimiter behavior).

I've attached a stub prompt set file (EdgeFin_prompt_set_v1.json) and a short benchmark harness README (redwood_benchmark_harness.md) showing how we plan to measure latencies and compute percentiles. If that looks good, can Vivek and I coordinate a test window next week?

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: EdgeFin: Performance SLO benchmark methodology - follow-up

Thanks Marissa — that recap matches our notes. A few clarifications and I attached our prompt set (EdgeFin_prompt_set_v1.json):

- Streaming: yes, we need token-level streaming to our frontend. We standardize on ~200ms chunk intervals in the UI; however p99 on token emission is the KPI.
- Input mix: ~60% short prompts (<100 tokens), 30% medium (100-512 tokens), 10% long (>512 tokens).
- Cold-starts: we see a small percentage of cold sessions (5-10%) when sessions are idle >30 minutes — include cold-start measurements if possible.
- Reproducibility: we can share a Google Drive folder with reference inputs and a small evaluation harness (we'll add the link).

We've uploaded the prompt set and a short CSV template (edgefin_benchmark_results_template.csv) to the drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3edgefin-eval-harness

Would next Tue (Aug 4) 09:00 PT work for an initial run? If you need Procurement on the call to cover data-sharing / NDAs let me know and I'll loop them in.

Best,
Laura

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeFin: Performance SLO benchmark methodology - follow-up

Perfect — thanks for sharing the prompt set and the drive link. A couple of notes on our side before the run: 

- Measurement definitions (we'll publish these in the harness README for reproducibility):
  * Request latency: time from request arrival at ingress to first-byte emitted (for streaming p50/p95/p99 reported on first-byte and last-byte).
  * Token emission latency: per-chunk time between server emit and client receive (we'll simulate the UI chunking).
  * Throughput: sustained RPS measured over 5-minute windows; report median and 95th windowed throughput.

- Warmup & reproducibility: we'll perform 3 warmup runs of 10 minutes each to stabilize kernel selection and cache; then 3 measured runs of 15 minutes. We'll seed the KV cache with a representative prefix set to emulate production priming.

- Concurrency matrix: can you confirm the concurrency buckets you'd like us to test (e.g., 10, 50, 120, 200 concurrent sessions)? We'll also run a short spike test to 300 concurrent sessions for graceful degradation behavior.

If Tue 09:00 PT works, we suggest an initial window for measurement and then a 30-minute sync to review the first-pass results. I'll attach the redwood_benchmark_harness.md with the exact commands (attached).

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_harness.md (attachment stub)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeFin: Performance SLO benchmark methodology - follow-up

Laura / team — quick technical points from the runtime side that will affect measurement reproducibility:

- Warmup specifics: our empirical tests show kernel selection stabilizes after ~5 minutes of sustained input for a given sequence-length distribution. In addition to your 3 x 10m warmup, we'll run a short single-run where we sweep sequence lengths to ensure kernels chosen are representative.
- Cold starts: we'll instrument and report cold-start latency separately. For a fair production-like run, please indicate if you want the cold-starts included in the p99 calculation or reported as a separate metric.
- KV cache priming: provide 100 representative session prefixes if you want to reproduce your prefix cache hit rates; otherwise we'll use the prompt set to infer prefix distribution which can bias results.
- Streaming measurement: we need a specified chunk size (eg. 64 tokens or 200ms interval). If you prefer timing-based chunking we'll simulate the 200ms interval you mentioned and will report per-chunk jitter.

One more ask: please provide the expected error-rate tolerance (e.g., 0.1% 500-level HTTP errors). We will also capture tail GC pauses and GPU migration events if they occur during the run.

Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@edgefin.com>

Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 17:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: EdgeFin: Performance SLO benchmark methodology - follow-up

Thanks Vivek — answers inline:

- Include cold-starts as a separate metric; p99 should reflect steady-state only.
- We'll provide 120 session prefixes (export attached to the Drive). Use your default 64-token chunk size but also run the timing-based 200ms simulation so we can compare.
- Error tolerance: target <0.5% 5xx across measured windows. If backpressure causes retries we want you to capture retry rates separately.

Aug 4, 09:00 PT works for the initial run. I'll share a calendar invite and add Procurement for the brief 30-min sync after the run. Link to drive again: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3edgefin-eval-harness

See you then — Laura
